headline: Highest risk is none-to-low overall: no shared channels, no writes, and no network egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading failure pathways largely blocked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a knowledge-management list with no I/O surfaces or execution path; agent B has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem, or MCP bridge. With no shared communication channel documented, there is no plausible default prompt-injection pathway between them.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies A's text into B's prompt, the risk becomes active.
IF either agent is connected to a shared clipboard or message queue, reassess as non-none.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared clipboard or queue bridges.
Do not paste A's content into B without sanitization.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags if an orchestrator later links them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither agent shows filesystem read/write, screen capture, clipboard, or network egress. A touches no data classes, and B's I/O surfaces are all false, so there is no documented path for sensitive data to flow from one agent to the other or out to a third party.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted filesystem access, re-evaluate leakage.
IF sensitive files are manually pasted into B, leakage risk becomes active.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in any manually supplied prompts.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls before enabling file ingestion.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is non-runnable and exposes no write or network capabilities; B cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. With no overlapping mutable resource access, there is no capability conflict pathway in the documented profiles.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk appears.
IF B is reconfigured to modify git state, reassess overlap.
mitigations: Do not place both agents on the same mutable workspace.
requires-engineering: introduce locking if shared writes are added later.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A does not produce an action-taking agent output; it is an awesome-list knowledge resource, and B is a document processor with no downstream action authority shown. Without a documented chain where B treats A as authoritative, cascading error is not plausible by default.
conditions: IF B is configured to auto-act on A's text, the pathway becomes active.
IF A's content is used as an unverified source in a downstream workflow, reassess upward.
mitigations: Require human review before any downstream action.
Do not auto-ingest A into B as authoritative input.
requires-engineering: add verification steps if automation is introduced.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and A touches no data classes while B's data_classes_touched is empty. With no compliance-relevant data flow shown, there is no identifiable residency or retention mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's workflow, reassess compliance.
IF deployment regions or retention policies diverge for shared data, the verdict changes.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy checks if data handling is added.
